claims.claim: chlorophyll breakdown in autumn unmasks yellow and orange carotenoids already present in the leaf
claims.definition: as days shorten, chlorophyll is actively broken down and its nitrogen resorbed; carotenoid pigments that were present through the growing season, previously masked by the dominant green chlorophyll, become visible
claims.measured_value: qualitative: yellow/orange autumn color is unmasked pre-existing carotenoid; no single-number claim
claims.authoritative_source: Hoch, Zeldin & McCown, 'Physiological significance of anthocyanins during autumnal leaf senescence', Tree Physiology 21 (2001); Lee, 'Anthocyanins in autumn leaf senescence', Advances in Botanical Research 37 (2002)
claims.notes: narration says 'pale carotenoids that were there all along finally show' — standard textbook account

nuance.note: carotenoid unmasking during chlorophyll breakdown is textbook plant physiology

claims.claim: red autumn color comes from anthocyanin synthesized fresh in the leaf during autumn, not from a hidden pigment
claims.definition: unlike carotenoids, anthocyanins are largely absent in green summer leaves of many species (e.g., red maples); in autumn they are actively synthesized from sugars in the cell vacuole during senescence
claims.measured_value: qualitative: autumn anthocyanin is newly synthesized from sugars during senescence; no single-number claim
claims.authoritative_source: Hoch, Zeldin & McCown, Tree Physiology 21 (2001); Feild, Lee & Holbrook, 'Why leaves turn red in autumn: the red flag for photoinhibition', Nature 410 (2001)
claims.notes: this is the story's core contradiction; 'brewed' is metaphor, mechanism stated plainly in B4

nuance.note: de novo anthocyanin synthesis during autumn senescence in red-coloring species is well documented (Hoch et al. 2001)

claims.claim: autumn conditions — trapped sugars, bright light, cool temperatures — drive anthocyanin synthesis in the leaf
claims.definition: during senescence, sugars remaining in the leaf (from reduced phloem export) plus light promote anthocyanin biosynthesis; bright, cool (but not freezing) autumn weather intensifies red coloration
claims.measured_value: qualitative: bright sunny and cool autumn conditions deepen red color; narration avoids thresholds
claims.authoritative_source: Feild, Lee & Holbrook, Nature 410 (2001); Hoch et al., Tree Physiology 21 (2001); standard plant-physiology treatments of anthocyanin biosynthesis regulation
claims.notes: narration deliberately avoids 'freezing' — cool, not cold, nights; no thresholds claimed

nuance.note: light and sugar promotion of anthocyanin synthesis is well established; exact regulatory details vary by species

claims.claim: one leading hypothesis is that anthocyanin protects the leaf's nutrient-recovery process from excess autumn light
claims.definition: photoinhibition hypothesis: anthocyanins attenuate incoming light within the leaf, reducing photoinhibition while chlorophyll is degraded and nitrogen and phosphorus are resorbed before leaf fall (Feild et al. 2001; Hoch et al. 2001)
claims.measured_value: qualitative: protective effect on nutrient resorption reported in several species; narration says 'one leading idea'
claims.authoritative_source: Feild, Lee & Holbrook, 'Why leaves turn red in autumn: the red flag for photoinhibition', Nature 410 (2001); Hoch et al., Tree Physiology 21 (2001)
claims.notes: narration hedges with 'One leading idea'; support varies by species and study

nuance.note: photoprotection has empirical support (Feild et al. 2001; Hoch et al. 2003) but its generality and relative importance are actively studied

claims.claim: why leaves synthesize anthocyanin remains debated: sunscreen, antioxidant, and pest-defense hypotheses all compete
claims.definition: proposed functions of autumn anthocyanin include photoprotection ('sunscreen'), antioxidant protection during senescence, and anti-herbivore signaling (e.g., Archetti's coevolution hypothesis); no single function is universally accepted
claims.measured_value: qualitative: multiple competing hypotheses; narration explicitly says 'It is not settled' and 'Scientists still argue'
claims.authoritative_source: Archetti, 'The origin of autumn colours by coevolution', Journal of Theoretical Biology 205 (2000); Lev-Yadun & Gould (eds.), 'Anthocyanins in Leaves', Advances in Botanical Research 37 (2002); Feild et al., Nature 410 (2001)
claims.notes: this beat exists to carry the contested mechanism honestly; every alternative is attributed as a hypothesis

nuance.note: genuine scientific debate: multiple hypotheses with partial support; the video must not present any one as settled
